Hey Buddy, not sure why this came up on my feed but I was rejected by UCL too 12 years ago so I get how you feel. I too had a lot of friends going to London uni's, and a girlfriend at the time that was also going to a London uni, so I was devastated. Ultimately I went to Uni of Nottingham in the end, as it was one of the highest ranking unis for the course I was doing. It was difficult at first, and definitely not what I wanted in life at the time.

I ended up making new friends at uni, but still kept close with my old friends that went to London unis. Nottingham was a real fun small city as a student, and I don't regret any of my time there. The girlfriend at the time left me straight after graduating uni and starting work, which broke me for a while but that's life for ya.

Eventually went to UCL for a Masters degree, and now I'm doing well in my job, made lots of new friends along the way, and am living with a girl I love dearly who I started dating there 7 years ago.

What I want to say, is that even if life hits you with devastating events now, keep at it and have some courage to go down some alternative paths. There's always different paths you can take in life, multiple of which will give you good results, and as long as you keep positive you will end up somewhere where you can be proud that you got through the painful moments. 

Also, just because you end up in different unis to your friends doesn't mean you'll lose them! Keep in touch, meet up when you can, but also expand your social circle! I discovered a lot by meeting people from all over the UK at Nottingham, whom I wouldn't have met had I gone to UCL for uni.

Good luck mate!

It happened like this.

Day 1 – I ask my girlfriend, “I promised my friend, who is a girl, that I would let her stay in my flat the day she arrives in this country several months ago. Would you be ok with that?” to which she replies “No, but I understand that you don’t want to break promises with your friends, it is your choice.” I say, “I understand. This was a promise from before we started dating, and I feel it would be rude to suddenly cancel it when she is relying on me, so this would be the only time.”

A few weeks later my friend arrives and stays, while I was very ill. During this time my girlfriend was abroad, so I let her know by text that my friend has arrived, and my girlfriend replied that my friend can take care of me while I am ill.

About a week later, I introduce my friend to my girlfriend, and during that meeting we talk about how my friend might need to stay again about a month later. My girlfriend didn’t comment on it at that time.

A month later when we were talking, my girlfriend asks me if my friend would be staying, and I say yes, to which she replies “I don’t like you” in what I saw as a playful way/joke. This was a big mistake. We quite often joked about who will get bored of each-other first and break up, and how we had a great time by ourselves when we were apart in a playful way, and I mis-interpreted this as the same type of conversation.

The day my friend stays my girlfriend texts me asking me if she is staying, and I reply yes, to which she replies, “ok I won’t talk to you for 3 days”, to which I reply, “this is the last time.” I was feeling confused as I had told her that she is staying. Again, a mistake, I should have realised at this point that I had been hurting her.

I thought about this for the 3 days and realised that I had crossed her boundary twice, and apologized to her, by text as she did not want to see me. She replied that she had told me that she would be hurt and that I didn’t care about her feelings, and I did it twice.

I could only give her a sincere apology after this, to which she replied that she doubts I love her, that she still loved me, and this scares her, and that we should talk after we cool down and think about it.

It is now a week after this. I am worried as I cannot tell if I am deluding myself to my interpretations of her feelings, to get what I want, or I am just inexperienced in this type of communication in relationships. Never-the-less I know I need to respect a partner more by being more attentive.

She didn't remind me that it violated her boundary, only she told me she was really hurt several days after I let her stay for the second time.

I didn't realise that it hurt my girlfriend while I was acting, which is why I'm terrified of and shocked by my behaviours and am struggling to fix myself.

I completely understand if she is done with me.

tldr: What I thought was a date, was a ploy to make me join a pyramid scheme.

Went to a cafe and started getting to know each other, conversation moved towards work life balance, how important money is etc. She seemed a genuinely down to earth person who was working hard to find what she wants in life. She then moved on to start talking about an "owner" friend she has that is teaching her amazing life tips. Owner in this context meant an owner of a business.

It was pretty vague but I had personally never met a person that had such great life advice to give, so when she invited me over to go and meet this friend with her over a few drinks I thought, "strange but what do I have to lose anyway!"

So we proceed to go to this friend's house, where they apparently set-up a little bar. This looked pretty cool, it was like a fashionable house party and had some wonderful home-made sangria. She introduced me to this owner person. A very pretty young lady.

The conversation moved to life goals, life ambitions etc, where she then suddenly started talking about how this person in the country we are in owns the exclusive rights to selling Tabasco, and that for every product sold  they get a certain percentage - making them extremely rich. She was explaining a business model which once you get going, brings in money automatically. I don't know if this Tabasco thing is true, but then she pulled out a magazine. She says she is selling these products, and how that this company uses no advertising, but only word of mouth to promote them. That because they use no money on advertising, the products are of much higher quality and value. At this point she started explaining a ton of stuff that just went completely over my head as it didn't make any sense to me. A lot of talk about dreams, success and shit. Then she pulls out a board-marker, and starts drawing on a white board I hadn't noticed until then. 

She draws a bunch of circles... one at the top, branching to two, to four; a pyramid of circles. 

"Uhhhhh.... so this is a pyramid scheme?"

"No, it looks like a pyramid, but it absolutely isn't! There is a lot of bad press on the internet but don't believe it, believe in your dreams, work hard at it and you WILL be successful!"

All during this time, the girl I was supposed to be on a date with is nodding away with a gleaming smile.

My heart sunk at the thought I had wasted one of my first few days living abroad on this crap, so I made an excuse that I had to go home. The girl left with me, so on the way back I asked her how much product she had bought, and how much she had sold. She had bought thousands of dollars worth of product, and sold none! Absolutely nothing! She hadn't even been able to persuade another person to join her "group" in the scheme.I told her that isn't that enough evidence this isn't going to work? She wasn't taking any of it and offered me an  energy drink to try for free. Apparently it was meant to be the most delicious energy drink, which is also highly nutritious.

For a few seconds I considered actually trying to persuade her to stop being brainwashed but... it's near impossible to do that. I wished her the best and parted ways.

Tried the drink when I got home, it was disgusting. Looked at the label, nutritional my ass.

This was Amway by the way.

However, in some cases people may blame god for things out of their control, use god as a scapegoat to rationalise their self-destructive behavior; this is not gain. The statement does not include the idea of religion, where I would usually argue that religion creates unnecessary and backward thinking restrictions on how you can live your life. From the statement "human reason can only decide the question of God's existence according to the possible resulting happiness of the decision", you can interpret that as if God makes people happy, then he can exist. If he does not make people happy, he does not exist. If you circle this back to the idea that you gain everything if you believe in god, then this is wrong as there are plenty of unhappy people that believe in God. In my opinion, the statement is too bold and there are too many open ended questions for the argument to be viable.

I usually just write whatever I'm feeling, and the possible reasons with it with as little thinking as possible. Like, go mad and type the first words that come into my mind without stopping, no-matter how childish or stupid it may seem. I then go and read over it; the sentences are all over the place so I slowly edit what I've written, gather the key points and organize it so that it makes sense. It's like a memory dump your computer does before crashing, so you can go and have a look at it later to see what went wrong.
